While I believe this story it doesn't make me feel that this shouldn't be the law. She will get her photo ID but will have to work through the Bureaucracy.

This article is an anecdote that illustrates something wrong with the way validation of eligibility to vote is happening in North Carolina.

It is still 100% defensible to validate that somebody is eligible to vote in an election before accepting and counting their vote in that election.

The name on her license doesn't match the name on her birth certificate. She has nothing other than her word to explain why. Yes, it's an extra step to prove who she is, but honestly, how is that DMV supposed to know what the truth is? Someone came in with documents that don't match and they're supposed to just accept it?

It's not that she can't get a valid ID in the new state, it's that they require proof of name change to accept her birth certificate as valid. The title is rather misleading.

That's a terrible argument to make against voter ID laws. You need an ID to get alcohol, you need it to open a bank account, you need it to buy a firearm (a protected right in the constitution). But we shouldn't require one to vote, which can affect others and isn't a protected right in the constitution?
